Typhoon Choi-wan has steadily moved northeast today, moving away 
from the far northern Mariana Islands. All tropical storm and typhoon
watches and warnings have ended and Typhoon Choi-wan will continue 
to move away from the region. In its place the monsoon surge will 
remain draped over the Marianas. A relative lull in shower activity 
is expected tonight through Tuesday with isolated to low-end (30%) 
scattered showers and isolated thunderstorms. The wet phase of the 
monsoon is expected to return Tuesday night as the monsoon 
reorganizes. There is potential for another round of heavy rainfall 
during the second half of this week and a hydrological products may 
be necessary. Another lull looks to develop late this weekend. 

Marine...
Hazardous marine conditions remain across the Marianas. Combined seas
range between 11 and 14 feet. A Gale Warning remains in effect until
10 PM for frequent gusts to 40 kt across Saipan and Tinian. By 10 PM
gusts are expected to decrease and become occasional. The Gale
Warning will be replaced with a Small Craft Advisory. Guam and Rota
are under a Small Craft Advisory until Tuesday afternoon. Surf
remains hazardous along north, west, and south facing reefs. Surf
will remain hazardous through at least Monday afternoon, but will
likely need to be extended in time. Seas look to quickly subside this
week, potentially becoming benign on Thursday night.

Tropical Systems...
Typhoon Choi-wan (26W) is currently located well north of the Maug 
Islands, near 23N147E. Choi-wan has been consuming high-octane ocean
fuel today, rapidly intensifying from a 90 knot mid-grade Category 2
storm early this morning to a powerful 125 knot Category 4 typhoon, 
nearly approaching super typhoon status. Choi-wan will continue to 
move away from the region and is forecast to exit our area of 
responsibility late tonight or Monday morning. Choi-wan will continue
to have an influence over the Marianas over the coming days as the 
monsoon surge remains locked over the region. Choi-wan will also 
produce a distant north swell that will help keep surf high the next 
few days. 

For more information on TY Choi-wan, see bulletins issued by the 
Joint Typhoon Warning Center (JTWC) under WMO header WTPN32 PGTW and
by the National Weather Service under WMO headers WTPQ32 PGUM and
WTPQ82 PGUM.

A developing disturbance known as Invest 94W by the Joint Typhoon 
Warning Center (JTWC) is located about 54 miles southwest of 
Kwajalein. Development is rated medium, meaning tropical cyclone 
development is likely beyond 24 hours. Scatterometry data indicates 
15 to 20 kt winds near Kwajalein, Ebadon, Ujae, Bikini, and Rongelap,
with winds up to 25 kt near heavier showers. Invest 94W will be 
generally slow to move, remaining over the northern Marshall Islands 
through Tuesday night. Scattered to numerous showers and isolated 
thunderstorms may lead to locally heavy rainfall and flooding. 
Through Friday, 4 to 6 inches of rain with locally higher amounts is 
possible.

Gusty winds and elevated, choppy seas will make marine conditions 
difficult. Residents may need to reconsider plans for inter-island 
boating as the week continues.

94W will continue to develop near Kwajalein over the next day or 
two, so residents in the northern Republic of Marshall Islands (RMI) 
should monitor the forecast for the next several days.

For more information on Invest 94W please see the JTWC header 
ABPW10. Also keep up to date with the latest information 
from your local emergency management agency.

Eastern Micronesia...
Invest 94W, which organized fairly quickly the last 24 hours,
continues to spin just north of Kwajalein. Convection continues to
try to wrap around the center, with the cyclonic flow strengthening
across the region. This has lead to increased surface convergence and
showers developing near Kosrae. We expect this trend to continue with
convective coverage also developing near Majuro overnight, and near
Pohnpei Monday night. As such, rainfall coverage/probabilities were
increased at Kosrae and Pohnpei. At Majuro, the forecast has
maintained scattered showers for a few days now and this looks good.
It's not out of the question that shower coverage may need to be
increased to numerous there with later forecasts, depending how
quickly 94W evolves towards a tropical depression. The current
thinking is this may hold off until late Monday night or Tuesday when
the system starts to pull away from the area to the north-northwest,
which would decrease rainfall potential.

As for marine conditions, the majority of the numerical guidance
increases the southwest winds wrapping into 94W, with guidance
suggesting sustained winds just shy of 22 knots, but with frequent
gusts above that starting later tonight and continuing through early
Tuesday morning at Majuro. As such, we hoisted a Small Craft
